Article Title: "I felt let down as a wife and as a mother": Has Gisele Bündchen spoken about why she ended her marriage to Tom Brady?

Has Gisele Bündchen spoken about Tom Brady’s focus on his career leading to their divorce?

Tom Brady, the seven time Super Bowl champion, was married to Brazilian supermodel Gisele Bündchen for thirteen years before they ended their marriage in 2022. While it has been a couple of years since their separation, neither Tom Brady nor Gisele Bündchen has spoken about the reason behind it.No, the former Victoria’s Secret model Gisele Bündchen has made no such claims about her marriage to the New England Patriots’ legend Tom Brady.A fanpage on X made a fake post that read as, “Gisele Bündchen reportedly opened up about the reasons behind the end of her marriage to Tom Brady, making several explosive claims about their relationship and family life. According to the statement, Gisele felt that Tom was often absent and failed to give their family the attention she believed they deserved.”The post added, “”I felt let down as a wife and as a mother watching everything unfold.” She also addressed accusations of infidelity and the difficult moments in their relationship, saying that resentment and regret eventually consumed their marriage. According to the claims, Gisele eventually gave Tom an ultimatum, asking him to prioritize either his family or his football career. “He made it clear that he had built his career long before I came into his life and that he wasn’t prepared to walk away from it, even for his family.That was when I realized I had to make a decision for myself.””The post is entirely fake as Gisele Bündchen has made no such claims about her divorce to Tom Brady.Months after their divorce, Gisele Bündchen sat for an interview with Vogue where she said the reason behind their divorce is not so “black and white”.Despite the post on X being fake, it has sparked a heated debate among fans.A fan took to X and wrote, “She finally said what a lot of people already knew. He built his whole identity around football, she built hers around the family they actually had, and when she asked him to choose, he chose the game.”Another fan posted, “That sounds like years of hurt and resentment building up. 💔 No matter how successful someone is, being present for your family matters too. Sometimes love alone isn’t enough when two people want different things from life.A third fan posted, “She’s called the ultimatum story hurtful rumor, said the split was more complicated than football vs. family, and that she has no regrets and still wants Tom to be happy.”Another fan noted, “This is recycled fake news. Gisele has already addressed these exact claims years ago and denied giving any ultimatum. She described the split as them growing apart, not this dramatic version. Same fabricated quotes keep getting reposted for engagement.”
Article Summary: A fanpage on x made a fake post that read as, “gisele bündchen reportedly opened up about the reasons behind the end of her marriage to tom brady.” according to the claims, gisele eventually gave tom an ultimatum, asking him to prioritize either his family or his football career.

NEW DELHI: Japan will face India in a historic men's T20I on September 22 at the Sano International Cricket Ground. India are the ICC Men's T20 World Cup champions and the No. 1 ranked side. Japan have already announced the squad that will take on India.The match will be Japan's first step in their preparation for the Asian Games in Nagoya, which begin two days later.Japan's all-time leading T20I run-scorer Kendel Kadowaki-Fleming will lead the team. Ibrahim Takahashi and Declan Suzuki-McComb are the other two players in the squad who have played more than 50 T20Is.The squad is the same group that Japan have picked for their Asian Games campaign.Japan have left out players who are eligible to play T20Is under ICC rules but cannot play at the Asian Games under its rules.This has opened the door for emerging spin-bowling all-rounder Jake Kusuda-Nairn, who impressed in domestic cricket.Spinner Tsuyoshi Takada also returns to the squad. He first played for Japan at the ICC East Asia-Pacific Twenty20 Championship in 2013.The squad includes Wataru Miyauchi and Makoto Taniyama, who studied at Japanese schools with cricket Bukatsu programs.Taniyama is a leg-spinner who developed his bowling action by watching Shane Warne videos on YouTube.He wears shirt number 23 in honour of the Australian great and is Japan's leading wicket-taker across pathway and international competitions.Charlie Hara-Hinze, who was part of Japan's U19 Cricket World Cup team that beat Tanzania, has also been included.Spinner Benjamin Ito-Davis is back after his East-Asia Pacific T20 World Cup 2028 Sub-Regional Qualifier campaign was cut short by a hand injury.Japan finished second in the East-Asia Pacific T20 World Cup 2028 Sub-Regional Qualifier.They remain in the race for qualification after finishing level on points with Papua New Guinea. Japan were edged on net run rate despite beating the Barramundis on the final day.The India-Japan match is the first step of “Sport 75”, an initiative that aims to promote human exchanges and cooperation between India and Japan through sport.The initiative comes from an agreement reached during a summit between Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.The agreement also took note of India's ambition to host the Olympic and Paralympic Games in 2036.Japan will play two T20Is against Hong Kong on September 19 and 20, before facing India on September 22.At the Asian Games, Japan will play Afghanistan on September 24 and Nepal on September 26.Japan need to finish in the top two to progress to the quarter-finals.Kendel Kadowaki-Fleming (c), Charlie Hara-Hinze, Benjamin Ito-Davis, Alester Kadowaki-Fleming, Kohei Kubota, Jake Kusuda-Nairn, Wataru Miyauchi (wk), Reo Sakurano-Thomas, Alex Shirai-Patmore (wk), Shoma Sugaya-Slater, Declan Suzuki-McComb, Tsuyoshi Takada, Ibrahim Takahashi, Makoto Taniyama, Lachlan Yamamoto-Lake.
Article Summary: India are the icc men's t20 world cup champions and the no. 1 ranked side. Match is the first step of ‘sport 75’, an initiative that aims to promote human exchanges and cooperation between india and japan through sport.

Coco Gauff, the 22 year old tennis legend, has been busy in the 2026 US Open as she has advanced to the quarterfinals while being seeded No. 4 in the tournament. As Coco Gauff prepares to go against reigning French Open champion and No. 5 seed Mirra Andreev, her comments on handling pressure have resurfaced.In an interview, the tennis legend Coco Gauff weighed in on her experience in the 2025 US as she said, “I cried on the court, everybody saw that. So yeah, that was the last time I cried. I think for me it just felt like so much pressure in that moment.”The World number 4 champion added, “But I’m kind of happy that I did it, because I felt like people got to see the vulnerability of being an athlete. And also because I created this agenda that I am calm, cool, and collected.”Coco Gauff continued, “And I don’t like when people say that, because it’s not true. So I got to show a little bit of that. But I would not want to feel like that again.”Over the last few years, Coco Gauff has been a force to be reckoned with on the court. The 22 year old star has made a name for herself and has often spoken about how both her parents have sacrificed their own careers to support her.For the unversed, Coco Gauff’s father became her primary tennis coach and gave up on his career in tennis to be by his daughter’s side.Both her parents are also often spotted attending all her matches and cheering her on as Coco Gauff has quickly turned into one of the most promising athletes in the world in the recent few years.A few hours ago, as Coco Gauff beat 18 year old American rising star Iva Jovic (6-1, 6-4) in an 80-minute showcase, she opened up about her win as she said, "Incredible player and incredible talent…”The 22 year old tennis star added, "Give it up for Iva … There was one game when I felt like I was running a marathon. First time I was out of breath on court in a long time."In an interview, Coco Gauff has also spoken about her inspiration as she said, “The WTA player that I admire the most is definitely Serena Williams. Why? I mean, she’s iconic. Everything to her on court fashion and how fierce a competitor she is, and just the representation that she presented for me. She’s an inspiration for me.” she said.

NEW DELHI: A toss before an India vs Pakistan match is always special. But one toss from 1984 has remained memorable for a very different reason.On April 13, 1984, India and Pakistan met at the Sharjah Cricket Stadium in the United Arab Emirates during the inaugural Asia Cup.India captain Sunil Gavaskar and Pakistan captain Zaheer Abbas were at the centre of a light-hearted moment before the match. As the toss took place, Gavaskar jokingly put his foot over the coin, creating a candid moment between the two captains.The match was part of the first-ever Asia Cup, which featured only three teams - India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.India won the toss and decided to bat first and scored 188/4 in 46 overs. Surinder Khanna was India's top scorer with 56 off 72 balls. Sandeep Patil added 43 off 50 balls. Gavaskar stayed unbeaten on 36 off 55 balls. Ghulam Parkar scored 22, while Dilip Vengsarkar made 14.Pakistan's bowlers picked up four wickets, with Shahid Mahboob, Mudassar Nazar and Sarfraz Nawaz among those to take wickets.Pakistan's chase never gathered momentum. They were bowled out for 134 in 39.4 overs.Mohsin Khan top-scored with 35, while Zaheer Abbas made 27.Qasim Umar scored 16 and Saleem Malik made 15, but Pakistan lost wickets regularly.India's bowlers played a major role in the collapse.Roger Binny and Ravi Shastri took three wickets each. Binny finished with 3/33, while Shastri returned figures of 3/40.Pakistan were eventually dismissed for 134, handing India a big victory.India went on to win the first Asia Cup title. The 1984 tournament had just three teams - India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.India have since become the most successful team in Asia Cup history based on the title record provided. India have won the tournament record nine times - 1984, 1988, 1990-91, 1995, 2010, 2016, 2018, 2023 and 2025.Sri Lanka have won the Asia Cup six times, while Pakistan have two titles.Bangladesh have finished runners-up four times, while Afghanistan's best result is a Super Four appearance.
Article Summary: India captain sunil gavaskar and pakistan captain zaheer abbas were at the centre of a light-hearted moment before the match. The match was part of the first-ever asia cup, which featured only three teams - india, pakistan and sri lanka. India have won the tournament record nine times - 1984, 1988, 1990-91, 1995, 2010, 2016, 2018, 2023 and 2025.

Article Title: LIV Golf bombshell: League files for bankruptcy owing up to $1bn; what happens now to its biggest stars?
Article Text:
FILE - A general view of the 18th hole flag pole during the first round of LIV Golf Jeddah at the Royal Greens Golf & Country Club, Friday, March 1, 2024 in King Abdullah Economic City, Saudi Arabia. (Matthew Harris/LIV Golf via AP, File)

Jon Rahm tops list of players owed money

LIV wants to return as a player-owned league

Players are not obliged to join LIV 2.0

Rahm and DeChambeau remain uncertain about their futures

Saudi Arabia's role is coming to an end

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A caddie studies the putting green at the 18th hole during the first round of the LIV Golf tournament in Naucalpan on the outskirts of Mexico City, Thursday, April 16, 2026. (AP Photo/Fernando Llano)

LIV Golf has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the United States, putting the future of the breakaway tour and its biggest stars into fresh uncertainty after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew its multibillion-dollar backing.The filing was made in federal court in New Jersey on Tuesday, with LIV saying the process will allow it to restructure its finances and pursue a new ownership model ahead of a planned return next year.But the court documents show the scale of the financial problems facing the tour. LIV estimates that it has between $500m and $1bn in liabilities owed to at least 1,000 creditors, while its estimated assets are between $100m and $500m.Among those creditors are several of LIV's biggest stars, with at least $45m owed to 14 current and former players included among the 30 largest unsecured claims.The filing now leaves players facing a major decision: whether to remain with a restructured version of LIV Golf or leave and attempt to recover money owed to them through the court process.The court documents detail the 30 largest unsecured claims against LIV Golf.Two-time major winner Jon Rahm has the largest claim among the players, with an unsecured claim of $7.5m.He is followed by Bryson DeChambeau, who is listed as being owed $5.7m, while Dustin Johnson has a claim of $5.5m.Australian Cameron Smith is listed at $4.8m and England's Tyrrell Hatton at $3.4m.The list also includes Brooks Koepka, despite the five-time major winner having already left LIV to return to the PGA Tour in January 2026. Koepka has an unsecured claim of $1.7m.In total, the 14 current and former LIV players among the 30 largest unsecured creditors are owed just over $45m.However, a source familiar with the figures told BBC Sport that the amounts listed represent money owed and not paid for the third quarter of 2026, rather than the full value of the players' contracts or the total amount they are owed.That distinction is important given the size of some of the contracts that helped LIV attract leading players away from established tours.According to reports, more than $5bn was spent by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund on LIV since the breakaway tour launched in 2021, with its first season taking place in 2022.Major champions including Rahm and DeChambeau were among the players attracted by lucrative contracts and large prize funds, helping LIV establish itself as a serious rival to the PGA Tour while also creating one of the biggest divisions the sport had seen in decades. Now, that original model is coming to an end.LIV's Chapter 11 filing does not mean the tour intends to disappear.Instead, the organisation says it wants to use the bankruptcy process to reorganise and return in a different form.LIV says it has identified BC Partners, an international investment firm, as its proposed new investor following the decision by Saudi Arabia's PIF in April to withdraw its funding.LIV chief executive Scott O'Neil said the court process would provide the structure and time needed to pursue the proposed transaction and begin the next stage of the league.“This process gives us the structure and time to pursue a landmark transaction and begin the next chapter of LIV Golf,” O'Neil said.He added that the proposed new version would be built around fans, a player-first ownership model and a place within the wider global golf ecosystem.LIV's letter to fans described the court-supervised restructuring as a way to address its previous financial obligations while completing the transaction intended to support the league's next phase.The organisation said the new league would be built around a “sustainable business model”, marking a significant change from the huge spending that defined LIV's early years.Players are expected to receive equity in the new organisation, while their individual commercial rights would be returned to them. That would give players greater opportunities to earn money away from prize funds.The proposed prize money would also be reduced.LIV says its purses would be lower than those on the PGA Tour, whose prize funds have increased in part because of the competition created by LIV, but would remain higher than events on the DP World Tour.There are also plans to change the competition itself.The proposed new league would expand fields to 75 players, introduce a cut, create qualifying events and add more teams that embrace national identities.LIV also wants those teams to develop into long-term global sports businesses rather than simply remaining golf teams attached to the tour.The organisation intends to start the new majority player-owned league early in 2027, although LIV said no definitive decisions had yet been made about the 2027 schedule or individual events.LIV had already laid off the majority of its staff this month, another sign of the change from the heavily funded first version of the tour.The biggest question is now whether the players who helped make LIV a global golf story will remain part of it.BBC Sport understands that players have no obligation to sign up to LIV 2.0, even if they previously signed multi-year contracts with LIV Golf.Sources have told BBC Sport that contracts under the previous version of LIV will end as a result of the court filing, with money owed to players and other creditors dealt with through the bankruptcy process.It remains unclear, however, when those players would be free to begin discussions with other tours.LIV said it remains in advanced discussions with players, including talks about creating an ownership structure that would align their interests with the league's long-term success.Several LIV stars have reportedly been linked with possible returns to the PGA Tour and other circuits.But a return to the PGA Tour is not currently straightforward.PGA Tour chief executive and commissioner Brian Rolapp has confirmed that the tour has no current plans to reinstate its Returning Member Program, meaning players such as Rahm, DeChambeau and Smith do not currently have a direct route back.That programme was previously used by Koepka when he returned to the PGA Tour in January.As part of that agreement, Koepka forfeited his LIV player equity shares for five years, lost eligibility for the $100m FedEx Cup bonus programme and agreed to make a $5m charitable donation.His return therefore came with significant conditions, and there is currently no indication that the same pathway will be reopened for the other LIV players.The uncertainty surrounding the biggest names was already visible before Tuesday's filing.At LIV's final event of the season in Indianapolis last month, O'Neil told the BBC he had “high levels of confidence” that the organisation could attract a critical mass of players to make the new league viable.DeChambeau was also positive about what could come next, saying there was “a lot of potential moving forward” and that he believed there was “something fun coming”.Rahm was more cautious.Speaking on Tuesday ahead of this week's Irish Open, the Spaniard was asked whether he knew what the coming months would bring.“Yes and no,” Rahm told BBC Sport.“It hasn't really changed from my last interview in Indianapolis.”He said there were many possible developments still ahead before adding: “Time's gonna tell.”Rahm also made clear that he was still prepared to fulfil his existing agreement with LIV.“I still have a contract with LIV 1.0 that I'm more than willing to fulfil, so like I said, time will tell,” he said.The bankruptcy filing has now changed the situation around those existing contracts, with BBC Sport reporting that the previous agreements will finish through the court process.LIV's financial difficulties follow the decision by the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia to stop funding the tour.PIF had invested an estimated $5bn (£3.7bn) into LIV since its launch, helping fund the contracts, prize money and infrastructure that allowed the new league to challenge the PGA Tour.When announcing its decision to withdraw funding in April, PIF said the “substantial investment required by LIV Golf over a longer term” was no longer consistent with its strategy.The fund nevertheless said it remained committed to its wider investments in sport.Despite withdrawing its backing, PIF is still providing LIV with $49.6m (£36.6m) in debtor-in-possession financing to help fund the bankruptcy process.LIV is also seeking recognition of its US bankruptcy filing in England and Wales, which would extend the protection to its international assets and operations.The Chapter 11 process gives a US company protection from creditors while it attempts to reorganise its debts or sell parts of its business.For LIV, that process is now being used to try to preserve the league rather than simply shut it down.The original LIV model, built on enormous Saudi investment and the recruitment of many of the world's biggest players, has reached its financial end.What emerges next is intended to be smaller, more sustainable and partly controlled by the players themselves, but whether the stars who made LIV what it became will still be there is yet to be decided.
Article Summary: Liv golf has filed for chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the united states. Saudi arabia's public investment fund withdrew its multibillion-dollar backing. Liv estimates that it has between $500m and $1bn in liabilities owed to at least 1,000 creditors. At least $45m owed to 14 current and former players included among the 30 largest unsecured claims.

Article Title: Ishan Kishan knocking on India door with Test case
Article Text:
East Zone's captain Ishan Kishan plays a shot on day 2 of the Duleep Trophy 2026-27 final cricket match between South Zone and East Zone, in Chennai. (PTI)

KOLKATA: East Zone skipper Ishan Kishan ’s monumental 270 off 334 balls in the Duleep Trophy final has strengthened his case for a return to the Indian Test side, with the Jharkhand wicketkeeper-batter now emerging as a genuine all-format option after an impressive run in international as well as domestic cricket.The innings against South Zone in Chennai was more than just a big score. Coming after a season in which Ishan has consistently delivered in both white-ball and red-ball cricket, it offered a strong indication that he has developed the temperament and game to succeed in the longest format.Former India wicketkeeper Saba Karim believes Ishan’s recent progress reflects a greater maturity in his approach to the game.“The work Ishan has put in at the domestic level over the last season reflects his growing maturity and his desire to be a part of Indian cricket across all three formats. It is good to see him understand his game better and keep improving. The hard work and introspection he has invested in his cricket are now showing in his performances,” Karim told TOI on Tuesday.The conditions made the 270 even more significant. Ishan spent more than nine hours over two days at the crease in Chennai’s heat and humidity, against a strong South Zone attack, to produce one of the most emphatic red-ball statements of his career.“To score 270 in a Duleep Trophy final against a strong South Zone side speaks volumes about his development as a red-ball cricketer. Doing it in Chennai, where the conditions are extremely hot and humid, makes the effort even more special. It was a remarkable innings and I am delighted for him,” Karim said.Former India batter Saurabh Tiwary , Ishan’s senior teammate for Jharkhand, believes the Duleep Trophy performance is a continuation of a broader resurgence rather than an isolated effort. Ishan has also been among the runs in the 2025-26 Ranji Trophy, his highest of the season being 173 from 247 deliveries against Tamil Nadu, in tough batting conditions in Coimbatore.“He has been doing well for some time now, and I can say he is having a golden touch,” Tiwary said. “What’s important is that he has performed not only in white-ball cricket but also in red-ball cricket.”That consistency has now put the Test door firmly within reach.“There is tremendous competition in the Indian team, and it’s never easy to secure a place, but he is certainly knocking on the door,” Tiwary said.Karim feels Ishan’s value to India goes beyond his wicketkeeping credentials, particularly given his ability to contribute in different roles.“Now, with the runs he has scored in red-ball cricket, the Indian team will certainly view him as a strong option in the Test format as well. If your batting is good enough, you can always earn a place as a specialist batter, even if you are primarily known as a wicketkeeper,” he said.The transformation has come through a return to the domestic grind following a season without a BCCI central contract.“One of the most important aspects of a cricketer’s career is responding to setbacks. If you are out of the team, you have to go back to domestic cricket, work hard and become the best performer you can be. Ishan has followed that path,” Karim said.
Article Summary: Ishan kishan's 270 off 334 balls in the duleep trophy final has strengthened his case for a return to the indian test side. The innings against south zone in chennai was more than just a big score. It offered a strong indication that he has developed the temperament and game to succeed in the longest format.

Kylie Kelce has never been shy about discussing the messy, funny and deeply personal parts of motherhood. On her “Not Gonna Lie” podcast, the mother of four recently turned to a subject many new parents may find awkward to discuss openly: intimacy after childbirth. Her comments mixed humor with a blunt reminder that recovery does not end when a baby arrives.During the March 26, 2026 episode of her podcast, Kylie Kelce spoke about what returning to s*x can feel like after giving birth. Her youngest daughter, Finn, was 11 months old at the time, giving the conversation a personal connection rather than making it a distant discussion about postpartum recovery.Kylie noted that people generally need to wait six to eight weeks before having s*x after childbirth, stressing that healing comes first.“You’re not even allowed to have s*x for six to eight weeks. She’s not ready cause she’s not healed,” Kelce said, while making clear that her comments were based on her experiences with vaginal births.She then delivered the kind of unfiltered observation that has become part of her podcast style.“I’ve had varying experiences, it’s different for every kid. It’s not all fun and games the first couple times, if you catch my drift.We can’t be out here like, ‘Oh that was great,’” she jokingly added. “A human just exited that door.”The joke landed because it captured something often left out of polished conversations about new motherhood. Childbirth can change the body in major ways, and physical recovery does not always follow a neat timetable.Kelce's willingness to say that out loud is part of what makes her discussions resonate. She does not present postpartum life as a smooth transition back to normal. Instead, she talks about the awkwardness, exhaustion and unexpected moments that come with raising children.Her comments also come with an important caveat. Postpartum recovery varies from person to person, and medical guidance should come from a qualified healthcare professional who understands an individual's circumstances.The conversation eventually moved beyond postpartum intimacy and into the bigger question of whether Kylie and Jason Kelce are finished expanding their family.For now, Kylie said that four children feels right. She is raising daughters Wyatt, Elliotte, Bennett and Finn with Jason, but she stopped short of making a permanent declaration about having another baby.“I will say Finny is still just cuddly enough that I do not have an urge for a baby right now," Kelce said. “I like to leave it open-ended, because I don’t want the universe to hear me or my uterus.”That playful uncertainty says plenty about her approach to motherhood. She can be content with where her family is while still leaving room for life to surprise her.And then there is Jason.When Kylie explained why people should not wonder too hard about the couple having four children, she turned the spotlight toward her husband’s post-NFL career.“Let me tell you something,” she quipped. “Don’t ever ask yourself why we have four kids. That’s self-explanatory. Turn on ESPN on Monday night.”Jason Kelce, who retired from the NFL and moved into broadcasting, has become a familiar presence on ESPN. Kylie’s joke offered a glimpse into the couple’s playful relationship while also giving listeners another example of the humor that runs through their family life.At its heart, Kylie Kelce’s conversation was not simply about sex after childbirth. It was about honesty. Motherhood can be beautiful and exhausting, intimate and uncomfortable, all at once. By talking about those contradictions without pretending they are glamorous, Kelce continues to make space for conversations that many parents experience but rarely discuss so openly.
Article Summary: Kylie kelce has never been shy about discussing the messy, funny and deeply personal parts of motherhood. Her comments mixed humor with a blunt reminder that recovery does not end when a baby arrives. Motherhood can be beautiful and exhausting, intimate and uncomfortable, all at once.

How the trade could impact the New Orleans Pelicans

Jordan Hawkins is heading to Memphis to join Cameron Boozer. The 24-year-old guard was dealt from New Orleans to the Grizzlies on Tuesday in a trade first reported by ESPN's Shams Charania, with forward Micah Peavy, a future second-round pick and a second-round pick swap also headed to Memphis. In return, the Pelicans land AJ Johnson and veteran forward Taj Gibson.The deal has roots in late July, when whispers first emerged that New Orleans was exploring trade frameworks to move Hawkins and create financial breathing room. Memphis, which has spent the past year hoarding draft capital and young talent, turned out to be the perfect landing spot.New Orleans had been shopping $20.6 million former UConn star Jordan Hawkins for weeks, according to Marc Stein and Jake Fischer of The Stein Line, who reported on July 22 that the Pelicans were working through trade frameworks to move him. Michael Scotto of HoopsHype added on July 31 that Johnson had entered those discussions as well. The pieces finally came together Tuesday.For New Orleans, the trade clears space to get Bennedict Mathurin's new contract on the books, a priority that made moving Hawkins almost inevitable. He still had one year and roughly $7 million left on his rookie deal, a manageable number that made him easy to move without much resistance.Memphis, meanwhile, keeps building its war chest. The Grizzlies now hold ten tradable second-round picks and twelve first-round picks across the next seven drafts, nine of which they can deal. Giving up AJ Johnson and Taj Gibson was a small price for a team this deep in assets.Hawkins lands in Memphis carrying more upside than his recent numbers suggest. The Pelicans picked him 14th overall in the 2023 draft, just three months after he helped UConn win a national championship. His rookie season showed flashes of that promise, averaging 7.8 points and shooting 36.6 percent from three across 67 games. His signature moment came against Dallas in January 2024, when he dropped a career-high 34 points in a Pelicans win.His role shrank after that. Last season he played just 51 games, started only once, and averaged 5.1 points in limited minutes. Even so, a career 37.4 percent shooter from the field has value, and Memphis is betting it can unlock the version of Hawkins that torched the NCAA Tournament at 50 percent from deep. If that shooter shows up, the Grizzlies just found themselves a bargain.For New Orleans, this trade is less about what they got and more about what it lets them do next. Offloading Hawkins' salary gives the front office room to lock in Bennedict Mathurin, a move that has been the underlying goal of these talks since July.AJ Johnson gives the Pelicans a young guard already familiar to their front office from earlier trade conversations, while Taj Gibson brings a steady, experienced presence to a locker room that could use one. Inside Dillon Jones' remarkable run to two championships

Dillon Jones is bringing his rings to Philadelphia. The 76ers signed the 24-year-old forward to an Exhibit 10 contract on Tuesday, ESPN's Dave McMenamin first reported, giving Jones a shot to win a training camp roster spot. Jones spent last season with the Knicks after winning a title with Oklahoma City the year before, making him one of the more unusual free-agent additions in the league this offseason.Philadelphia already added Jaylen Brown and LeBron James this summer, and Jones now joins a growing list of new faces chasing a championship the Sixers have not lifted in decades. He also reunites with Ariel Hukporti, his former Knicks teammate, giving Philadelphia two players who know exactly what it feels like to hoist a trophy.The Sixers made the news official on Tuesday, announcing Dillon Jones' signing in a press release after ESPN's Dave McMenamin broke the news first. "Back-to-back champ Dillon Jones signed with the 76ers to an Exhibit 10 contract," McMenamin wrote, adding that Jones would join Philadelphia's training camp later this month.An Exhibit 10 deal carries no guarantees. It simply gives Philadelphia a low-risk window to evaluate Jones before deciding whether to convert him to a two-way contract or send him to the Delaware Blue Coats.For a player who has bounced through three organizations in two years, it is a familiar kind of audition.Jones gives Philadelphia size and versatility at forward, standing 6-foot-5 and 235 pounds with the strength to guard multiple positions. His NBA numbers do not jump off the page. Across 61 combined games with Oklahoma City and New York, he has averaged just 2.4 points, 2.1 rebounds and 1.0 assist in under ten minutes a night.His G League work tells a different story. Jones averaged 15.2 points, 6.1 assists and 5.6 rebounds in 18 games for the Westchester Knicks last season, shooting close to 38 percent from three after making just 27.5 percent the year before. This kind of jump is exactly what earned him a senior-year MVP award in the Big Sky Conference, where he averaged 20.8 points, 10.1 rebounds and 5.2 assists at Weber State.If that shooting holds up, Philadelphia may have found a legitimate developmental piece buried inside a camp contract.Jones barely played in either title run, appearing in just seven games and 39 minutes for the Knicks and none of them in the playoffs. Coach Mike Brown still leaned on him during the postseason. "I spoke to Dillon often during this playoff run," Brown said on The Roommates Show, explaining that Jones had just gone through a similar run with Oklahoma City.

Article Title: True Samaritans: Indian volunteers take up grim task of cleaning decomposed bodies in Kathmandu
Article Text:
Volunteers of Hemkunt Foundation cleaning floors of a morgue in Kathmandu. (PC: Hemkunt Foundation)

DEHRADUN:

As rescue agencies continue recovering bodies from flash flood-hit areas in Nepal and bringing them to Kathmandu mortuaries, a group of young Indian volunteers has taken up a task few are willing to do — cleaning decomposed bodies before they are handed over to families and authorities for the last rites. The group has helped clean more than 30 bodies till now.At least seven volunteers -- Harteerath Singh, Neha Singh, Jag Singh, Jaskaran Singh, Ravi Singh, Amitose Singh and Harry Singh -- of Hemkunt Foundation, a Gurgaon-based non-profit organisation, are carrying out the work at the morgue of Maharajgunj Medical Campus, Kathmandu.One of the volunteers, Neha Singh, told TOI Friday that she travelled from Mumbai to Kathmandu for the voluntary service after coming across a social media post by the foundation, requesting volunteers to join them in Nepal. “The next thing I did was to fly down to Kathmandu without expecting anything,” she said, adding that volunteers were not known to each other before reaching there; and were now working as a family in this ‘sewa’ (selfless service).They say that they are totally focused on the task, and even the terrible stench of bodies has failed to deter them. Neha said, “We are here for the respect of the departed souls and the bereaved families.We don’t seek any publicity in that.”Another member of the group, Harteerath Singh, elaborated on some of the challenges being faced by them. “Due to the acute stench, sometimes, it becomes unbearable for us to stand inside the morgue even for a minute,” he pointed out.“But this is the ultimate ‘sewa’. At times, we don’t even bother to wear masks or gloves. We cover our faces with one corner of the turban cloth and just go inside to clean the bodies and floors of the morgue -- something which even the local authorities may not be willing to do,” Singh said.“We also see the positive side of it. It is the biggest opportunity for us to serve humanity.”
Article Summary: At least seven volunteers of hemkunt foundation, a gurgaon-based non-profit organisation, are carrying out the work at the morgue of maharajgunj medical campus, kathmandu. They say that they are totally focused on the task, and even the terrible stench of bodies has failed to deter them.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Fyodor Dostoevsky: "Your worst sin is that you have destroyed and…" - a powerful reminder to ask what you are really gaining from every sacrifice
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Fyodor Dostoevsky (Image: Wikipedia)

Quote of the day by Fyodor Dostoevsky

"Your worst sin is that you have destroyed and betrayed yourself for nothing"

Where this line actually comes from

What is the meaning of Fyodor Dostoevsky’s quote

Why this quote still genuinely matters today

The real difference between sacrifice and genuine self-betrayal

Know what genuinely matters to you

Do not confuse approval with genuine happiness

Think honestly about the cost of your choices

Learn to recognise when enough is genuinely enough

Other famous quotes by Fyodor Dostoevsky

"Man only likes to count his troubles; he doesn't calculate his happiness."

"Above all, don't lie to yourself. The man who lies to himself and listens to his own lie comes to a point that he cannot distinguish the truth within him, or around him, and so loses all respect for himself."

"To go wrong in one's own way is better than to go right in someone else's."

"Taking a new step, uttering a new word, is what people fear most."

How to apply this quote in daily life

Why this timeless message still resonates

This line is one of the most quoted passages from Fyodor Dostoevsky's Crime and Punishment, and it captures something genuinely powerful about self-betrayal, regret and the choices people make when they lose sight of what actually matters to them. Unlike many quotes about failure that focus on losing money or opportunity, this line points at something considerably more personal, the real damage a person can do to themselves by repeatedly acting against their own values. It is especially relevant in a world where people often feel real pressure to fit in, please others, or simply appear successful. Someone may stay in a situation that genuinely makes them unhappy purely because they fear disappointing another person. Another may quietly give up an ambition simply because it never seemed practical enough to pursue properly, and yet years later they may find that the compromise achieved nothing at all worth having.The quote comes from Part 4, Chapter 4 of Crime and Punishment, first published in 1866, and it is worth being genuinely accurate about its actual context. The line is not Dostoevsky speaking directly in his own voice. It is dialogue spoken by the character Svidrigaïlov, a genuinely unsettling and morally complicated figure in the novel, to Sonia, a young woman who has been forced into desperate circumstances to support her family.The fuller passage reads, "But you are a great sinner, that's true, and your worst sin is that you have destroyed and betrayed yourself for nothing. Isn't that fearful? Isn't it fearful that you are living in this filth which you loathe so, and at the same time you know yourself that you are not helping any one by it, not saving any one from anything." Dostoevsky, as the author, crafted this scene specifically to explore themes of guilt, sacrifice and self-destruction that run throughout the entire novel, and the line has genuinely outlived its original scene, circulating today as a standalone reflection on self-betrayal more broadly.The real meaning here lies in the words "destroyed" and "betrayed." This is not describing an ordinary mistake. It describes what happens when someone repeatedly goes against their own conscience or their own values. To genuinely betray yourself can mean knowing exactly what you actually believe while choosing to act differently anyway, out of fear, pressure or simple convenience. It can happen gradually, rather than through one single dramatic decision. Someone may genuinely know that a particular friendship is unhealthy but keep maintaining it because they do not want to be alone. These decisions can feel necessary in the moment, but if they continue for too long, a person can genuinely begin to feel disconnected from who they actually are. The second half of the line, "for nothing," sharpens the whole message. Sacrificing yourself for a genuine purpose is a very different thing from destroying yourself for something that ultimately carries no real value at all.Modern life creates countless real opportunities for people to compare themselves against each other. Social media and constant professional competition can make it genuinely tempting to change yourself simply to gain approval. People can spend years chasing a career purely because it looks impressive from the outside, even while it genuinely leaves them unhappy. This line encourages a genuinely different kind of self-examination instead. Before making a major compromise, it is worth honestly asking what exactly is being sacrificed, and what is actually being gained in return.Not every difficult choice actually means a person is betraying themselves. People regularly make genuine sacrifices for their children, their families or a long-term goal, and the important question is always whether the sacrifice genuinely serves something meaningful. Self-betrayal happens when a person keeps abandoning what actually matters to them without any clear purpose behind it, constantly saying yes when they genuinely want to say no, or giving up an important ambition purely out of fear of other people's opinions. A useful distinction is this: genuine sacrifice should take you somewhere. Self-betrayal can leave you feeling like you have lost yourself without gaining anything real in return.People can make genuinely poor decisions when they do not have a clear sense of their own values. Knowing what actually matters most makes it considerably easier to recognise when a situation is asking you to compromise too much.Being accepted by absolutely everyone is genuinely impossible. Constantly changing yourself to satisfy other people can eventually leave you genuinely unsure about what you actually want for yourself.Every major decision genuinely involves a trade-off. Before making a real sacrifice, it helps to consider both sides honestly, asking what you are actually giving up and whether the result is genuinely worth it.Persistence is genuinely valuable, but persistence in the wrong situation can become quietly damaging. Walking away from something that repeatedly harms your sense of self is not always failure. Sometimes it is genuinely self-respect instead.This message does not require any dramatic change. It can genuinely begin with small acts of honesty instead. Before agreeing to something, it helps to ask whether you genuinely want to do it, or whether you are simply afraid of disappointing someone else. When considering a career decision, it helps to think beyond salary or prestige and ask whether the work actually fits the life you genuinely want. The same principle applies to relationships too. If you repeatedly have to hide your feelings or pretend to be someone else simply to keep a relationship functioning, it may be worth genuinely examining what that relationship is actually costing you.This line from Crime and Punishment is ultimately about the genuine value of remaining true to yourself. Life will always involve genuinely difficult decisions and real compromise, and the goal was never to avoid every situation that causes discomfort. The deeper lesson is understanding why you are actually making a sacrifice, and whether it genuinely serves something meaningful. "Your worst sin is that you have destroyed and betrayed yourself for nothing" works as both a warning and a genuine reminder. Before sacrificing an important part of yourself, it helps to pause and ask what you are actually gaining in return.
Article Summary: Quote of the day by fyodor dostoevsky. "your worst sin is that you have destroyed and betrayed yourself for nothing" "to go wrong in one's own way is better than to go right in someone else's" not every difficult choice actually means a person is betraying themselves.

Article Title: Chinese ‘League of Legends’ star Jian ‘Uzi’ Zi-hao retired at 25 after chronic wrist and arm injuries; researchers claim esports teams are now turning to physical therapists and trainers
Article Text:
Representative Image

The strain of 'climbing the ladder'

Preventative measures

Looking to the stage

A return to the stage

Chinese esports player Jian "Uzi" Zi-hao was more than a star "League of Legends" player. He was so talented that his team built its entire strategy around him, funnelling resources to him and another teammate, Shi "Ming" Sen-Ming, so the duo could lead the team to victory. Over the course of his career, he earned more than $500,000 in tournament prize money. However, in 2020, Jian announced his retirement after chronic wrist and arm injuries cut his storied career short. At that time, he was just 25 years old.Video games have a reputation for keeping people glued to the couch. But for those who compete against the best players in the world, gaming can be surprisingly physically and mentally taxing.The best esports players often have grinding schedules. They're expected to practice regularly, participate in scrimmages, and compete in official matches. Even at the recreational level, esports players cite the mental toll: playing hours a day, every day, to hone their skills and "climb the ladder."A 2021 study of Portuguese esports players found that 37% experienced anxiety and depression, and 45% experienced sleep disturbances.The most common physical injuries in esports generally fall under eye problems and musculoskeletal issues.Prolonged screen time leads to many vision problems in gamers, from common eye fatigue to decreased focus. Furthermore, screen light appears to contribute to sleep disturbances by disrupting the release of melatonin, the hormone that helps regulate the sleep-wake cycle.Many esports players, professional or otherwise, also battle hand and wrist pain, with repetitive button-smashing causing injuries such as carpal tunnel syndrome, tendonitis and "gamer's thumb," which arises from overuse or irritation of the tendons around the thumb and wrist. Many of the overuse injuries seen among video game players are also familiar to assembly-line workers, whose jobs can involve similarly repetitive movements.Then there are the back injuries. Players can remain seated for three or more hours without a break, and this prolonged sitting can take a toll on the lower back and spine.The sedentary nature of esports has also led to a lesser-known, sometimes fatal, injury called deep vein thrombosis: a blood clot, often in the leg, that can become life-threatening if it travels to the lungs. In 2011, British gamer Chris Staniforth, who would play for as long as 12 hours at a time, died of the condition.As more esports injury research has been published, more treatment and prevention strategies have emerged. Top esports teams now have physical therapists, performance psychologists, athletic trainers, and even massage therapists on staff to optimise their players' performance and recovery.Teams often incorporate group exercise activities to build rapport among players and reduce injury risk. During competition, proper positioning of the spine and limbs has become an essential injury prevention strategy. For example, selecting a chair that encourages an upright posture can reduce pain and injury risk, especially when gamers couple ergonomics with an exercise program that centers on functional strength, mobility and stretching of the upper limbs.When esports began gaining mainstream popularity in the 1990s and early 2000s, proponents were eager to compare it to traditional sports and athletic competition. The parallels helped establish esports' legitimacy and gave non-gamers a familiar framework for understanding the competition.As esports became a big business and a lucrative career path, players and teams hired a web of support staff, including trainers, coaches and therapists, that mirrored the structure of professional sports. In this vein, much esports injury research draws on the training methods of traditional sports.However, according to one exercise science scholar, injury treatment and prevention strategies could be further improved by viewing esports competitors more like musicians and dancers than football and basketball players.Performance optimisation and injury research on professional performing artists has existed for centuries, and the scholar argues it represents a valuable, untapped resource. This is because the physical and mental stresses of musical performance overlap with esports competition: long stretches of sitting, small dexterous hand movements, and performing without real-time input from a coach.For example, biomechanics research has found similar patterns of forearm muscle fatigue among esports players and piano players. However, no studies to date have directly compared the two groups.Researchers have also raised the possibility of applying interest in joint hypermobility or hand size among performing artists to esports populations, and whether popular piano warm-up exercises could be effective for esports athletes who use keyboards. Even research on sports like car racing might offer valuable insights, since, as with gamers, many people overlook how physically demanding car racing can be, including the extended periods of sitting it requires.Prevention and rehabilitation techniques keep improving. Even Jian, the player who retired in 2020, returned to play for a few splits, or partial seasons, in 2022 and 2023.In July 2023, "League of Legends" star Lee "Faker" Sang-hyeok was sidelined with cubital tunnel syndrome, an injury caused by arm and hand overuse. Through a treatment plan that included changing his gaming posture and intensive physical therapy, Lee was able to return to play just a month later. He went on to win three consecutive world championships, with his support team helping prevent injury recurrence throughout each season.Thanks to his rehabilitation, Lee's fans can follow his hunt for his fourth "League of Legends" World Championship, which kicks off in October 2026 in the US.
Article Summary: Chinese esports player jian "uzi" zi-hao announced his retirement in 2020. Chronic wrist and arm injuries cut his storied career short. Gaming can be surprisingly physically and mentally taxing. The most common physical injuries in esports generally fall under eye problems and musculoskeletal issues.
